data.dynamic_line: <get_lost>

dynamic_line.no:
Hey, who the fuck are you?  I haven't seen you 'round.  Ah, fuck it, it doesn't matter.
Here's the rules.  The first and most important one: ALWAYS CLOSE THE FUCKING ENTRY DOOR BEHIND YOUR ASS!  If you're okay with that, the following rules are: don't fuck with us, don't steal from us, don't start a fight without a reason with someone from us.  Got it, punk?  Now get lost.
dynamic_line.yes: <get_lost>

responses.text: Yeah, I got it.  See ya.
I just wanted to ask if you have a job for me.
I'm just hungry, and I thought you might give me some food for some job.
Can we just talk it over?

dynamic_line.no: Do I have a <swear> exclamation sign over my <swear> head, like I'm a <swear> quest-giver from some <swear> video game?
dynamic_line.yes: <get_lost>

responses.text: No, of course not!  Sorry, I'm leaving.

dynamic_line.no: <get_lost>
dynamic_line.yes: Are you deaf or stupid?  I said I don't give a fuck for you and your <swear> problems.  Bother me one more time, and you'll regret that.  <get_lost>

responses.text: Ok, sorry, I promise I won't bother you anymore.

data.dynamic_line: You think you're immortal, huh, <name_b>?

responses.text: Gee, what's the matter with you?  Okay, okay, I'm leaving.
It would be you who will regret talking to me like that.

dynamic_line: Not so fast, I think you need to pay for breaking your promise and bothering me.  Give me your shit, now!

responses.text: Please don't hurt me!  Take all that you want.

dynamic_line.yes: I have nothing more to say to you.  <get_lost>

no.yes: So, what are you waiting for?

I don't know if you know, but there are sewers underneath the prison.  I was planning an escape long before <the_cataclysm>, and while I was working on cleaning the sewers, I noticed a damaged wall section.  There was a flow of fresh air coming out of it, so I think it's leading to the surface.  It could be your way to freedom.  Feel free to use it.

yes.yes: You are what you eat, as they say.

no.no: Hello there.  Haven't seen you around before.  You must be from the other wing.  Managed to survive, huh?

responses.text: Yeah, I've been through situations far worse than that.
It was a nightmare, lots of <zombies>, blood everywhere!  Thank god I'm among living people again.
[Cannibal] It's hard to die of hunger when there's so many tasty corpses lying around.
I want to get out of this <swear> prison.  I hoped you could help me with that.
I don't know if I'll take your advice, but thanks nevertheless.
Wait, what?  A <swear> can of beans?!  I went through hell to get this <swear> thing for you, and all you give me as reward is a <swear> can of beans?!  I demand something more substantial.

dynamic_line: Huh, even so?  I'm not saying I approve your… tastes, but I definitely respect people who use all possibilities life has to offer.

responses.text: Yeah, we share the same opinions on this matter.

dynamic_line: Well, that's a boastful statement.  Not that I don't believe it, it's just….  Ah, nevermind.  Let's get to the point.  What do you want?

responses.text: I want to get out of this <swear> prison.  I hoped you could help me with that.

dynamic_line: Hold the horses, pal.  Nobody allowed you to stay here - yet.

responses.text: Please!  I don't want to go back there!  I'm tired and hungry!  I just need time to rest!
Shit!  Looks like I'm on my own now.  Thanks for nothing.  Bye.

dynamic_line: We don't have much space, and there's not much food.  Besides, I don't know you at all, and something tells me you won't survive another day.

responses.text: I guess I need to find some other place…

dynamic_line: The answer is still no.  In fact it might be better for us to kill you right away - you know, the less mouths to feed, the better.  But I'm in a good mood today, so I've decided to help you get out of this island.

responses.text: You know, I think I'll manage without your help.  Bye.

dynamic_line.no: I need you to retrieve some stuff from a locked safe.  Interested?
dynamic_line.yes: So, what are you waiting for?

responses.text: [Show the military id card] You mean this stuff?
What for do you need it?
I have a bad feeling about this.  Sorry, I'll pass.

dynamic_line: As I said, that's the thing I need.  You don't need to know what's that exactly.  Just grab all things you find in the safe, and call it a day.

responses.text: I have a bad feeling about this.  Sorry, I'll pass.

dynamic_line: Let's say that's none of your <swear> business.  Other questions?

responses.text: I have a bad feeling about this.  Sorry, I'll pass.

dynamic_line: Hey, where did you get it?  Nevermind, just give it to me.  Just <swear> now.

responses.text: Hey, no need to be hostile.  Here you go, I don't need it anyway.
I went through incredible hardships to get it.  Please, can I keep this to myself?
I killed tons of <zombies> while I was trying to get this thing.  Do you really think you and your handful of losers pose a threat to me?

dynamic_line: Okay.  It was convincing.  I'll still get what I want, one way or another.  You better watch your back from now on.
I'm afraid you're not in the position to demand anything from me, <name_b>.  <get_lost>

name.str: Get The Thing from the chief's office

dialogue.offer: My snitch whispered in my ear that the thing I need is located in the chief's safe in his office.  You need to crack it open and bring the contents to me.  Don't try to use anything you find in there!  Just bring all the stuff to me, and I'll help you.  Deal?
dialogue.accepted: Great!  Don't forget that I need all stuff from the safe, try not to lose a thing.
dialogue.rejected: Fine, I'll get the thing in any case, sooner or later.
dialogue.advice: The chief's office is on the other side of the prison.  I think the road there is full of <zombies>, so you better find a weapon.  Also you probably will need some tools to crack the safe open.
dialogue.inquire: Did you get the stuff already?
dialogue.success: At last!  Give me a few moments to check if it isn't damaged.  Here, take this for your troubles.
dialogue.success_lie: Huh.  This isn't going to work like I thought.
dialogue.failure: You're useless.  I should've killed you when I met you.

dialogue.describe: You wouldn't believe what I found…
dialogue.offer: Holy hell, the crash you recovered the black box from wasn't as old as I thought.  Check this out, it was on its approach to pick up a team sent to secure and destroy something called a 'Hazardous Waste Sarcophagus' in the middle of nowhere.  If the bird never picked up the team then we may still have a chance to meet up with them.  It includes an access code for the elevator and an encoded message for the team leader, I guess.  If we want to join up with what remains of the government then now may be our only chance.
dialogue.accepted: Fuck ya, America!
dialogue.rejected: Are you going to forfeit your duty when the country needs you the most?
dialogue.advice: If there is a military team down there then we better go in prepared if we want to impress them.  Carry as much ammo as you can and prepare to ditch this place if they have a second bird coming to pick them up.
dialogue.inquire: Having any trouble following the map?
dialogue.success: We got this shit!
dialogue.success_lie: What?!  I out'ta whip your ass.
dialogue.failure: Damn, we were so close.

dialogue.offer: I'm asthmatic.  I need you to get an inhaler for me…
dialogue.accepted: Oh, thank god, thank you so much!  I won't last more than a couple of days, so hurry…
dialogue.rejected: What?!  Please, <ill_die> without your help!
dialogue.advice: There's a town nearby.  Check pharmacies; it'll be behind the counter.
dialogue.success: Oh thank god!  I'll be right as rain in no time.
dialogue.success_lie: What?!  You're lying, I can tell!  Ugh, forget it!
dialogue.failure: How am I not dead already?!

dialogue.offer: I'm infected.  Badly.  I need you to get some good antibiotics for me…
dialogue.accepted: Oh, thank god, thank you so much!  I won't last more than a couple of days, so hurry…
dialogue.rejected: What?!  Please, <ill_die> without your help!
dialogue.advice: There's a town nearby.  Check pharmacies; it'll be behind the counter, either antibiotics or broad-spectrum antibiotics will do.
dialogue.success: Oh thank god!  I'll be right as rain in no time.
dialogue.success_lie: What?!  You're lying, I can tell!  Ugh, forget it!
dialogue.failure: How am I not dead already?!

dialogue.describe: We've got the flag, now we need to locate US forces.
dialogue.offer: We have the flag but now we need to locate US troops to see what we can do to help.  I haven't seen any but I'm figure'n one of those choppers that were fly'n round during th' outbreak would have a good idea.  If you can get me a black box from one of the wrecks I'll look into where we might open'er at.
dialogue.accepted: Fuck ya, America!
dialogue.rejected: Do you have any better ideas?
dialogue.advice: Survivors were talking about them crashing but I don't know where.  If I were a pilot I'd avoid crash landing in a city or forest though.
dialogue.success: America, fuck ya!
dialogue.success_lie: What?!  I out'ta whip you're ass.
dialogue.failure: Damn, I'll have to find'er myself.

dialogue.describe: With the black box in hand, we need to find a lab.
dialogue.offer: Thanks to your searching we've got the black box but now we need to have a look'n-side her.  Now, most buildings don't have power anymore but there are a few that might be of use.  Have you ever seen one of those science labs that have popped up in the middle of nowhere?  Them suckers have a glowing terminal out front so I know they have power somewhere inside'em.  If you can get inside and find a computer lab that still works you ought to be able to find out what's in the black box.
dialogue.accepted: Fuck ya, America!
dialogue.rejected: Do you have any better ideas?
dialogue.advice: When I was play'n with the terminal for the one I ran into it kept asking for an ID card.  Finding one would be the first order of business.
dialogue.success: America, fuck ya!  I was in the guard a few years back so I'm confident I can make heads-or-tails of these transmissions.
dialogue.success_lie: What?!  I out'ta whip you're ass.
dialogue.failure: Damn, I maybe we can find an egg-head to crack the terminal.

dialogue.offer: I hope you will find use from what you got out of the deposit box but I also have another job for you that might lead you to an opportunity to deal out justice for those who cannot.  First things first, we can't just look like ruffians.  Find us a deputy badge, easy enough?
dialogue.accepted: I'd check the police station.
dialogue.rejected: We're also official… just hang in there and I'll show you what we can really do.
dialogue.advice: They shouldn't be that hard to find… should they?
dialogue.success: Great work, Deputy.  We're in business.
dialogue.success_lie: Thanks for trying…  I guess.
dialogue.failure: The day of reckoning will come for the criminals if it hasn't already.

dialogue.describe: Does our flag still yet wave?
dialogue.offer: Does our flag still yet wave?  We're battered but not yet out of the fight, we need the old colors!
dialogue.accepted: Hell ya!  Find me one of those big ol' American flags.
dialogue.rejected: Seriously?  God damned commie…
dialogue.advice: Find a large federal building or school, they must have one.
dialogue.success: America, fuck ya!
dialogue.success_lie: What?!  You liar!
dialogue.failure: You give up?  This country fell apart because no one could find a good man to rely on… might as well give up, I guess.

dialogue.offer: Our world fell apart because our leaders were as crooked as the con-men that paid for their elections.  Just find me one of those corporate accounting books and I'll show you and the rest of the world just who is at fault.
dialogue.accepted: You'll see, I know I'm right.
dialogue.rejected: I know it isn't pressing but the big corporations didn't get a chance to destroy the evidence yet.
dialogue.advice: Try a big corporate building of some sort, they're bound to have an accounting department.
dialogue.success: Great, let's see… uh… hmmm…  Fine, I didn't even do my own taxes but I'm sure this will prove their guilt if we get an expert to examine it.
dialogue.success_lie: Thanks for trying…  I guess.
dialogue.failure: The day of reckoning will come for the corporations if it hasn't already.

dialogue.describe: I hope I don't see many names I know…
dialogue.offer: I've lost so many friends… please find me a patient list from the regional hospital or doctor's office.  I just want to know who might still be out there.
dialogue.accepted: Thank you, I suppose it won't change what has already happened but it will bring me closure.
dialogue.rejected: Please, I just want to know what happened to everyone.
dialogue.advice: I bet you'll run into a lot of those things in the hospital, please be careful.
dialogue.success: Oh dear, I thought Timmy would have made it…
dialogue.success_lie: Thanks for trying…  I guess.
dialogue.failure: I bet some of them are still out there…

dialogue.describe: I wonder if a retreat might exist…
dialogue.offer: Everyone who dies gets back up, right?  Which means that whatever is causing this it must be airborne to have infected everyone.  I believe that if that is the case then there should be regions that were not downwind from where-ever the disease was released.  We need to find a record of all the weather patterns leading up to the outbreak.
dialogue.accepted: Thanks so much, you may save both of us yet.
dialogue.rejected: Ya, it was a long shot I admit.
dialogue.advice: I'm not sure, maybe a news station would have what we are looking for?
dialogue.success: These look more complicated than I thought, just give me some time.
dialogue.success_lie: This isn't what we need.
dialogue.failure: If only we could find a great valley or something.

dialogue.describe: St. Michael the archangel defend me in battle…
dialogue.offer: As the world seems to abandon the reality that we once knew, it becomes plausible that the old superstitions that were cast aside may have had some truth to them.  Please go and find me a religious relic…  I doubt it will be of much use but I've got to hope in something.
dialogue.accepted: I wish you the best of luck, may whatever god you please guide your path.
dialogue.rejected: Ya, I guess the stress may just be getting to me…
dialogue.advice: I suppose a large church or cathedral may have something.
dialogue.inquire: Any luck?  Please find me a small relic.  Any relic will do.
dialogue.success: Thank you, I need some time alone now…
dialogue.success_lie: What good does this do us?
dialogue.failure: It was a lost cause anyways…

dialogue.offer: Now I don't mean to upset you but I'm not sure what I can do with the accounting ledger at the moment.  We do have a new lead though, the ledger has a safe deposit box under the regional manager's name.  Guess what, dumb sucker wrote down his combination.  Come with me to retrieve the box and you can keep any of the goodies in it that I can't use to press charges against these bastards.
dialogue.accepted: You may make a tidy profit from this.
dialogue.rejected: I know it isn't pressing but the world is going to be just as corrupt when we start rebuilding unless we take measure to stop those who seek to rule over us.
dialogue.advice: This shouldn't be hard unless we run into a horde.
dialogue.success: Great, anything I can't use to prosecute the bastards is yours, as promised.
dialogue.success_lie: Thanks for trying…  I guess.
dialogue.failure: The day of reckoning will come for the corporations if it hasn't already.

dialogue.describe: Oh man, I can't believe I forgot to download it…
dialogue.offer: There's some important software on my computer that I need on USB.
dialogue.accepted: Thanks!  Just pull the data onto this USB drive and bring it to me.
dialogue.rejected: Seriously?  It's an easy job…
dialogue.advice: Take this USB drive.  Use the console, and download the software.
dialogue.inquire: So, do you have my software yet?
dialogue.success: Excellent, thank you!
dialogue.success_lie: What?!  You liar!
dialogue.failure: Wow, you failed?  All that work, down the drain…

dialogue.describe: It could be very informative to perform an analysis of zombie blood…
dialogue.offer: I need someone to get a sample of zombie blood, take it to a hospital, and perform a centrifuge analysis of it.
dialogue.accepted: Excellent.  Take this blood draw kit; once you've produced a zombie corpse, use it to extract blood from the body, then take it to a hospital for analysis.
dialogue.rejected: Are you sure?  The scientific value of that blood data could be priceless…
dialogue.advice: The centrifuge is a bit technical; you might want to study up on the usage of computers before completing that part.
dialogue.inquire: Well, do you have the data yet?
dialogue.success: Excellent!  This may be the key to removing the infection.
dialogue.success_lie: Wait, you couldn't possibly have the data!  Liar!
dialogue.failure: What a shame, that data could have proved invaluable…

dialogue.describe: St. Michael the archangel defend me in battle…
dialogue.offer: You have no idea how interesting this diary is.  I have two very promising leads…  First things first, the Catholic Church has been performing its own investigations into global cult phenomenon and it appears to have become very interested in a local cult as of recently.  Could you investigate a location for me?  I'm not sure what was going on here but the priest seemed fairly worried about it.
dialogue.accepted: I wish you the best of luck, may whatever god you please guide your path…  You may need it this time more than the past excursions you have gone on.  There is a note about potential human sacrifice in the days immediately before and after the outbreak.  The name of the cult is believed to be the Church of Starry Wisdom but it is noted that accounts differ.
dialogue.rejected: Ya, I guess the stress may just be getting to me…
dialogue.advice: I doubt the site is still occupied but I'd carry a firearm at least…  I'm not sure what you might be looking for but I'm positive you'll find something out of the ordinary if you look long enough.
dialogue.inquire: I'm positive there is something there… there has to be, any luck?
dialogue.success: Thank you, your account of these… demonic creations proves the fears the churches had were well founded.  Our priority should be routing out any survivors of this cult…  I don't known if they are responsible for the outbreak but they certainly know more about it than I do.
dialogue.success_lie: What good does this do us?
dialogue.failure: It was a lost cause anyways…

dialogue.describe: St. Michael the archangel defend me in battle…
dialogue.offer: I have another task if you are feeling up to it.  There is a prisoner that the priest made special mention of.  I was wondering if you could see what may have happened to him or if he left anything in his cell.  The priest admits the individual is rather unstable, to put it lightly, but the priest personally believed the man was some kind of repentant visionary.  I'm not in a position to cast out the account just yet… it seems the man has prophesied events accurately before concerning the Church of Starry Wisdom.
dialogue.accepted: I wish you the best of luck, may whatever god you please guide your path…  I can only imagine that the prison will be a little slice of hell.  I'm not sure what they would have decided to do with the inmates when they knew death was almost certain.
dialogue.rejected: Ya, I guess the stress may just be getting to me…
dialogue.advice: The worst case scenario will probably be that the prisoners have escaped their cells and turned the building into their own little fortress.  Best case, the building went into lock-down and secured the prisoners in their cells.  Either way, navigating the building will pose its own difficulties.
dialogue.success: Thank you, I'm not sure what to make of this but I'll ponder your account.
dialogue.success_lie: What good does this do us?
dialogue.failure: It was a lost cause anyways…

dialogue.describe: Well damn, you must be the guys here to pick me up…
dialogue.offer: I got the brief so I know what I'm getting into.  Let me be upfront, treat me like shit and I'm going to cover my own hide.  However, you treat me well and give me something to believe in, even if it's just a shiny bit of metal, and I'll do you right.  Without a strong band a man doesn't stand a chance in this world.  You ready to take charge boss?  This world could use a Sheriff just about now.
dialogue.accepted: Before we get into a major fight just make sure we have the gear we need, boss.
dialogue.rejected: I don't think you're going to find many other survivors who haven't taken up a faction yet.
dialogue.advice: I'm a pretty good shot with a rifle or pistol.
dialogue.success: Wait… are you really making me a deputy?
dialogue.success_lie: I don't think so…
dialogue.failure: Quitting already?

dialogue.describe: You seem to know this new world better than most…
dialogue.offer: You're kitted out better than most… would you be interested in making this world a little better for the rest of us?  The towns have enough supplies for us survivors to start securing a foothold but we don't have anyone with the skills and equipment to thin the masses of undead.  I'll lend you a hand to the best of my ability but you really showed promise taking out that other beast.  You, I, and a 100 zombies laid to rest, what do you say?
dialogue.accepted: Hell ya, we may get ourselves killed but we'll be among the first legends of the apocalypse.
dialogue.rejected: Hey, I know I wouldn't volunteer for it either… but then I remember that most of us survivors won't make it unless someone decides to take the initiative.
dialogue.advice: I'd secure an ammo cache and try to sweep a town in multiple passes.
dialogue.success: Man… you're a goddamn machine.  It was a pleasure working with you.  You know, you may just change our little neck of the world if you keep this up.
dialogue.success_lie: I don't think that was quite a hundred dead zeds.
dialogue.failure: Quitting already?

dialogue.describe: I've heard some bad rumors so I hope you are up for another challenge…
dialogue.offer: Apparently one of the other survivors picked up on an unusually dense horde of undead moving into the area.  At the center of this throng there was a 'leader' of some sort.  The short of it is, kill the son of a bitch.  We don't know what it is capable of or why it is surrounded by other zombies but this thing reeks of trouble.  Do whatever it takes but we can't risk it getting away.
dialogue.accepted: I'll lend you a hand but I'd try and recruit another gunslinger if you can.
dialogue.rejected: What's the use of walking away, they'll track you down eventually.
dialogue.advice: Don't risk torching the building it may be hiding in if it has a basement.  The sucker may still be alive under the rubble and ash.
dialogue.success: May that bastard never get up again.
dialogue.success_lie: I don't think we got it yet.
dialogue.failure: Quitting already?

dialogue.describe: The eater of the dead… something was ripping zombies to shreds and only leaving a few scattered limbs…
dialogue.offer: A few days ago another survivor and I were trying to avoid the cities by staying in the woods during the day and foraging for gear at night.  It worked well against the normal zed's but one night something caught onto our trail and chased us for ten minutes or so until we decided to split up and meet-up back here.  My buddy never showed up and I don't have the means to kill whatever it was.  Can you lend a hand?
dialogue.accepted: Thanks, make sure you're ready for whatever the beast is.
dialogue.rejected: Hey, I know I wouldn't volunteer for it either.
dialogue.advice: I'd carry a shotgun at least, it sounded pretty big.
dialogue.success: You look a little shaken up, I can't tell you how glad I am that you killed it though.
dialogue.success_lie: Something in the shadows still seems to stare at me when I look at the woods.
dialogue.failure: I'm glad you came back alive…  I wasn't sure if I had sent you to your death.

dialogue.describe: Oh god, I can't believe it happened…
dialogue.offer: My mom… she's… she was killed, but then she just got back up… she's one of those things now.  Can you put her out of her misery for me?
dialogue.accepted: Thank you… she would've wanted it this way.
dialogue.rejected: Please reconsider, I know she's suffering…
dialogue.advice: Find a gun if you can, make it quick…
dialogue.inquire: Well…?  Did you… finish things for my mom?
dialogue.success: Thank you.  I couldn't rest until I knew that was finished.
dialogue.success_lie: What?!  You're lying, I can tell!  Ugh, forget it!
dialogue.failure: Really… that's too bad.

dialogue.describe: I just need a place to start over…
dialogue.offer: I've accepted that everyone I used to know is dead… one way or another.  I really wish I could have done something to save my brother but he was one of the first to go.  I'd like to start over, just rebuild at one of the farms in the countryside.  Can you help me secure one?
dialogue.accepted: Thank you, let's find a remote one so we don't have to worry about many zombies.
dialogue.rejected: Please, I just don't know what to do otherwise.
dialogue.advice: Traveling the backroads would be a good way to search for one.
dialogue.inquire: Shall we keep looking for a farm house?
dialogue.success: Well, my adventuring days are over.  I can't thank you enough.  Trying to make this place self sustaining will take some work but the future is looking brighter.  At least it ought to be safe for now.  You'll always be welcome here.
dialogue.success_lie: Thanks for trying…  I guess.
dialogue.failure: I guess it was just a pipe dream.

dialogue.describe: Maybe they escaped to one of the camps…
dialogue.offer: I can't thank you enough for bringing me the patient records but I do have another request.  You seem to know your way around… could you take me to one of the FEMA camps?  I know some were overrun but I don't want to believe all of them could have fallen.
dialogue.accepted: Thank you, just bring me to the camp…  I just want to see.
dialogue.rejected: Please, I don't know what else to do.
dialogue.advice: We should go at night, if it is overrun then we can quickly make our escape.
dialogue.inquire: Any leads on where a camp might be?
dialogue.success: I guess this wasn't as bright an idea as I thought.
dialogue.success_lie: Thanks for trying…  I guess.
dialogue.failure: I bet some of them are still out there…

name.str: Reach The Mansion And Finish This Delivery

data.description: You were flying towards a nearby private airport before your forced landing.  You could still reach it by ground, and scavenge it for fuel.

dialogue.describe: St. Michael the archangel defend me in battle…
dialogue.offer: From what I understand, the creatures you encountered surrounding this relic were unlike anything I've heard of.  It is laughable that I now consider the living dead to be part of our ordinary reality.  Never-the-less, the church must have some explanation for these events.  I have located the residence of a local clergy man, could you go to this address and recover any items that may reveal what the church's stance is on these events?
dialogue.accepted: I wish you the best of luck, may whatever god you please guide your path.
dialogue.rejected: Ya, I guess the stress may just be getting to me…
dialogue.advice: If the information is confidential the priest must have it hidden within his own home.
dialogue.success: Thank you, a diary is exactly what I was looking for.
dialogue.success_lie: What good does this do us?
dialogue.failure: It was a lost cause anyways…

dialogue.describe: You seem to know this new world better than most…
dialogue.offer: We've got another problem to deal with but I don't think we can handle it on our own.  So, I sent word out and found us a volunteer… of sorts.  He's vain as hell but has a little skill with firearms.  He was supposed to collect whatever he had of value and is going to meet us at a cabin in the woods.  Wasn't sure how long we were going to be so I told him to just camp there until we picked him up.
dialogue.accepted: Rodger, if he's a no-show then any other gunslinger will do… but I doubt he'll quit before we even begin.
dialogue.rejected: Hey, I know I wouldn't volunteer for it either… but then I remember that most of us survivors won't make it unless someone decides to take the initiative.
dialogue.advice: I hope the bastard is packing heat… else we'll need to grab him a gun before we hit our next target.
dialogue.success: Great, just let me know when you are ready to wade knee-deep in an ocean of blood.
dialogue.success_lie: I don't think so…
dialogue.failure: Quitting already?

dialogue.offer: I left my poor dog in a house, not far from here.  Can you retrieve it?
dialogue.accepted: Thank you!  Please hurry back!
dialogue.rejected: Please, think of my poor little puppy!
dialogue.advice: Take my dog whistle; if the dog starts running off, blow it and he'll return to your side.
dialogue.inquire: Have you found my dog yet?
dialogue.success: Thank you so much for finding him!
dialogue.success_lie: What?!  You're lying, I can tell!  Ugh, forget it!
dialogue.failure: Oh no!  My poor puppy…

name.str: Break into armory to retrieve family photo

dialogue.describe: I need you to get my family photo from the armory safe.
dialogue.offer: I left the only photo I have from my family in the armory.  I don't have the code, can you get in?
dialogue.accepted: Thanks, it's great to see someone willing to help a out.
dialogue.rejected: Well, I'll find someone else to do it for me, real shame with all those guns locked up too…
dialogue.advice: You look like a resourceful sort, maybe you can hack it or something.
dialogue.inquire: Got the photo?  Should've been in my gun safe.
dialogue.success: Thanks!  I'll be sure to put in a good word for you around town.
dialogue.success_lie: OK, then hand it over.
dialogue.failure: Shit happens.

dialogue.offer: Show me the proof of your loyalty to the great Foodplace, and I'll consider you worthy of my friendship.  Ten loyalty cards should be enough, I'm sure you already have much more than that waiting for you at home, right?
dialogue.accepted: That's the spirit!  Good luck kid.
dialogue.rejected: That's alright not everyone is cutout for this.
dialogue.advice: Those are very precious, people would probably keep them on their person or in bank vaults.  And definitely not throw them in the trash!
dialogue.inquire: How is it going?  Do you have them?
dialogue.success: YES!  I knew you could do it!  You proved your worth and I'm proud to call you a friend.
dialogue.success_lie: Well…  where are they?
dialogue.failure: I'm so disappointed in you kid…

data.description: Prove you're a survivor by surviving for 10 days after the Cataclysm, and then returning to the person who gave you this mission.

dialogue.describe: It's hard to tell who actually has the skills to survive these days…
dialogue.offer: It's hard surviving out here on our own, and we'd probably have a better chance working together.  Problem is, I don't really know you and what you're capable of.  You might have what it takes, or you might not.  Either way, I'm going to need some proof.  Come back in a few days and I'll gladly follow you.  It's basically a win-win for me: either you come back and I'll know you've got what it takes, or you don't and I'll know that I was right not to follow you.
dialogue.accepted: I'll see you then… or I won't, and then I'll know I made the right decision.
dialogue.rejected: Ya, it was a long shot I admit.
dialogue.advice: Don't die.  If you're asking me for advice, that doesn't bode well for you.
dialogue.success: I'll be honest, I wasn't really expecting to see you again.  A promise is a promise, I'll follow you now!
dialogue.success_lie: I know time is relative and all that.
dialogue.failure: I'm not quite sure how you failed to survive AND are talking to me.

name.str: Gather cattail stalks to create cattail jelly

data.description: Gather <color_light_blue>80 cattail stalks</color> from the swamp and bring them back to <color_light_red>learn how to craft cattail jelly</color>.  Raise your <color_light_blue>survival skill to at least 1</color> by harvesting cattail stalks.  <color_light_blue>Bring back the provided bag</color> as well.

dialogue.describe: Medical services are a little sparse following <the_cataclysm>, but people have been surviving using their wits and the bounty of Mother Nature for a long time.  Care to learn a little?
dialogue.offer: Did you know that cattails are a source of a jelly that works as an antiseptic and analgesic?  Something like that is likely to be mighty helpful out here.  I want you to take this bag, head to the nearest swamp, collect 80 cattail stalks, and bring them back here.  In exchange, I'll show you how to harvest the jelly.
dialogue.accepted: Great!  This bag should be big enough to hold all of the stalks we'll need.  Don't forget to bring it back.
dialogue.rejected: Your loss.
dialogue.advice: The cattails grow in the fresh water in swamps.  You can't miss them.
dialogue.inquire: Got those cattail stalks yet?  Don't forget to bring back my bag and improve your survival skill to at least 1 as well.
dialogue.success: Great!  Hand them over and I'll show you how this works.
dialogue.success_lie: OK, then hand them over.
dialogue.failure: Well, that's a shame.

data.//: Commander in Necropolis

dynamic_line.yes: Marshal, I hope you're here to assist us.

no.u_male: Sir, I don't know how the hell you got down here but if you have any sense you'll get out while you can.
no.no: Ma'am, I don't know how the hell you got down here but if you have any sense you'll get out while you can.

responses.text: What are you doing down here?
Can you tell me about this facility?

data.dynamic_line: I'm leading what remains of my company on a mission to re-secure this facility.  We entered the complex with two dozen men and immediately went about securing this control room.  From here I dispatched my men to secure vital systems located on this floor and the floors below this one.  If we are successful, this facility can be cleared and used as a permanent base of operations in the region.  Most importantly it will allow us to redirect refugee traffic away from overcrowded outposts and free up more of our forces to conduct recovery operations.

This facility was constructed to provide a safe haven in the event of a global conflict.  The vault can support several thousand people for a few years if all systems are operational and sufficient notification is given.  Unfortunately, the power system was damaged or sabotaged at some point and released a single extremely lethal burst of radiation.  The catastrophic event lasted for several minutes and resulted in the deaths of most people located on the 2nd and lower floors.  Those working on this floor were able to seal the access ways to the lower floors before succumbing to radiation sickness.  The only other thing the logs tell us is that all water pressure was diverted to the lower levels.

responses.text: Whatever they did it must have worked since we are still alive…

dialogue.offer: My communications team went to secure the radio control room after we breached the facility.  I haven't heard from them since, I need you to locate them.  Their first objective was to record all active channels that were transmitting information on other survivors or facilities.  Find them and return the frequency list to me.  I'm sure they could probably use your help also.
dialogue.accepted: Good luck, the communications room shouldn't be far from here.
dialogue.rejected: I don't know why you would bother wasting your time down here if you can't handle a few small tasks…
dialogue.advice: We were briefed that the communications array was on this level.
dialogue.success: Thanks, let me know when you need another tasking.
dialogue.success_lie: What good does this do us?
dialogue.failure: It was a lost cause anyways…

dialogue.offer: Your assistance is greatly appreciated, we need to clear out the more ruthless monsters that are wandering up from the lower levels.  If you could cull twenty or so of what we refer to as 'nightmares' my men would be much safer.  If you've cleared out most of this floor then the lower levels should be your next target.
dialogue.accepted: Good luck, finding a clear passage to the second level may be tricky.
dialogue.rejected: I don't know why you would bother wasting your time down here if you can't handle a few small tasks…
dialogue.advice: These creatures can swing their appendages surprisingly far.
dialogue.success: Thanks, let me know when you need another tasking.
dialogue.success_lie: What good does this do us?
dialogue.failure: It was a lost cause anyways…

data.//: In charge of outside communications in Necropolis

dynamic_line.yes: Marshal, I'm rather surprised to see you here.

no.yes: Sir you are not authorized to be here… you should leave.
no.no: Ma'am you are not authorized to be here… you should leave.

responses.text: [MISSION] The captain sent me to get a frequency list from you.

data.dynamic_line: We are securing the external communications array for this facility.  I'm rather restricted in what I can release… go find my commander if you have any questions.

responses.text: I'll try and find your commander then…

data.dynamic_line: I was expecting the captain to send a runner.  Here is the list you are looking for.  What we can identify from here are simply the frequencies that have traffic on them.  Many of the transmissions are indecipherable without repairing or replacing the equipment here.  When the facility was being overrun, standard procedure was to destroy encryption hardware to protect federal secrets and maintain the integrity of the comms network.  We are hoping a few plain text messages can get picked up though.

dialogue.offer: My chief responsibility is to monitor radio traffic and locate potential targets to secure or rescue.  The majority of radio repeaters are down and those that are working have only emergency power.  If you have a basic understanding of electronics you should be able to fabricate the 'radio repeater mod' found in these plans.  When this mod is attached to a radio station's main terminal, all short range radio traffic on emergency channels is boosted so we can pick it up at much longer ranges.  I really need you make me one.
dialogue.accepted: Thanks, I know the labs on the other side of the complex have electronic parts sitting around.
dialogue.rejected: I don't know why you would bother wasting your time down here if you can't handle a few small tasks…
dialogue.advice: I'm sure the motorpool has a truck battery you could salvage.
dialogue.inquire: Have you had any luck fabricating it?
dialogue.success: Thanks, I'll see to installing this one.  It will be some time but I could use someone to position these around the region.
dialogue.success_lie: What good does this do us?
dialogue.failure: It was a lost cause anyways…

dialogue.offer: I guess I could use your skills once again.  There are small transmitters located in the nearby evacuation shelters; if we don't separate them from the power grid their power systems will rapidly deteriorate over the next few weeks.  The task is rather simple but the shelters offer us a place to redirect refugees until this vault can be secured.
dialogue.accepted: Thanks, I should be ready for you to install the radio repeater mods by the time you get back.
dialogue.rejected: I don't know why you would bother wasting your time down here if you can't handle a few small tasks…
dialogue.advice: Try searching on the outskirts of towns.
dialogue.inquire: Have you had any luck severing the connection?
dialogue.success: We are good to go!  The last of the gear is powering up now.
dialogue.success_lie: What good does this do us?
dialogue.failure: It was a lost cause anyways…

dialogue.offer: Most of my essential gear has been brought back online so it is time for you to install your first radio repeater mod.  Head topside and locate the nearest radio station.  Install the mod on the backup terminal and return to me so that I can verify that everything was successful.  Radio towers must unfortunately be ignored for now, without a dedicated emergency power system they won't be useful for some time.
dialogue.accepted: I'll be standing by down here once you are done.
dialogue.rejected: I don't know why you would bother wasting your time down here if you can't handle a few small tasks…
dialogue.advice: If you could make some sort of directional antenna, it might help locating the radio stations.
dialogue.inquire: Have you had any luck finding a radio station?
dialogue.success: That's one down.
dialogue.success_lie: What good does this do us?
dialogue.failure: It was a lost cause anyways…

dialogue.offer: I could always use you to put another repeater mod up.  I don't have to remind you but every one that goes up extends our response area just a little bit more.  With enough of them we'll be able to maintain communication with anyone in the region.
dialogue.accepted: I'll be standing by.
dialogue.rejected: I don't know why you would bother wasting your time down here if you can't handle a few small tasks…
dialogue.advice: Getting a working vehicle is going to become important as the distance you have to travel increases.
dialogue.inquire: Have you had any luck finding a radio station?
dialogue.success: I'll try and update the captain with any signals that I need investigated.
dialogue.success_lie: What good does this do us?
dialogue.failure: It was a lost cause anyways…

dialogue.rejected: What?!  Why do you… ah, forget it.
dialogue.advice: Maybe we can find some gasoline at gas station.

dialogue.rejected: What?!  Why do you… ah, forget it.
dialogue.advice: I heard that these 'restaurants' use some kind of locking system for staff room, so we would need to find a way to get there.
dialogue.success: Another one bite the dust!  We did good, <name_g>.

data.description: Help pizzaiolo take back his restaurant.

dialogue.rejected: What?!  Why do you… ah, forget it.

responses.text: [BARTER] Is that the lowest you can go?  I'd love some bread, but I can't quite make that.
[BARTER] Aw, c'mon.  I rescued Landough, can't you cut me a little deal?
Thanks, can we talk about something else?
I'll look into that.  I'd better get going though.

data.dynamic_line: Sorry, it's not something I can bend on.  I don't make a big profit off this, I use what I get to make more bread.  If I cut you a deal, I'll run out of supplies.
data.//: see above for responses to buy bread at original price.

responses.text: Well, I tried.  Can we talk about something else?
Thanks, but I think I'll pass.  I gotta run.

data.dynamic_line: Oh, fine.  Six cups of flour, or one merch.  I'm not going any lower, I got a business to run here.

responses.text: You know, I think I changed my mind.  Can we talk about something else?
I guess I'm outta here then.

data.dynamic_line: That's kind of you to say.  I'm doing my best to move on… it hurts, but in the scale of things it could be worse.  Pablo and I still have each other, that's a lot more than most.

responses.text: I'd better get going.  Bye, Dana.

yes: Great, here's a loaf of the best damn sourdough bread in the world.  I used to make that claim as a joke, but I feel like now there's a fighting chance nobody else can beat me.
Nice.  Enjoy the mighty bounty of Landough Calrisean.
Here you go, from the family recipe.
Hope you enjoy it as much as I do, this is the best damn bread in the world now.
dynamic_line.no: Great, here's a loaf of my locally-famous, not-very-mature sourdough.  It's not too bad honestly.  Everyone here seems to like it.

responses.text: You seem pretty unhappy about the quality of your bread.  Is there something I can do to help?
Thanks, can we talk about something else?
It smells awesome.  I'm going to head out now, thanks!

data.dynamic_line: Sorry, not quite yet.  Landough was in pretty rough shape.  No fault of yours, it was no good having him cooped up in a dank fridge for that long… and I think my apprentice baker may have fucked with him before the Cataclysm too.  He'd better hope he's a zombie now, because if I see him alive… anyway, it's gonna take a few more feeds before I can get him ready for prime time, check back in a couple days.

responses.text: I'd better get going.  Bye, Dana.

data.dynamic_line: Things are tense at the best of times.  We didn't choose this crowd, so not all of us really get along.  I like Jenny and Fatima, and the three of us are kind of lucky to have friends here, but that doesn't make up for us being a bunch of unfamiliar faces crammed into a tiny space.  Someone's gonna murder someone soon, mark my words.

responses.text: I'd better get going.  Bye, Dana.

dynamic_line.no: Huh.  I've made a few friends here, but not so much as I'd stick around here with no future prospects, hoping someone downstairs dies to make room for me.  It does sound nice, if they're looking for more workers.
dynamic_line.yes: Have you heard anything back from the ranch about jobs yet?

responses.text: I spoke to the foreman over at Tacoma Ranch.  If you're willing to put in the work, they'll find some work for you over there.
I'll look into that.  What were you saying before?
I'll look into that.  I'd better get going though.

data.dynamic_line: All right.  I've taken some time to think about it, and I'm willing to go.  I'm sure they'll have use for a baker over there, after all, and if I don't get out of this place there's a very real chance I'm going to snap.  You can go let Pablo know first hand, if you want; he's been pretty excited about the idea.

responses.text: Sure, I'll go tell him.  What were you saying before?
Sure, I'll go tell him.  I'd better get going though.

data.dynamic_line: Pablo's a little quicker on the trigger than I am.  We're trying to have a baby, did you know that?  It's a bit crazy in this world, but I won't change those plans.  Tell you what: if your camp has access to a doctor and some medical facilities, in case I actually can get pregnant again, I would consider getting out of here and signing up.

responses.text: I'll look into that.  What were you saying before?
I'll look into that.  I'd better get going though.

dialogue.describe: I could get my real sourdough starter…
dialogue.offer: If you really like this second-rate bread, you could risk your life for something actually worth it.  I left my actual sourdough starter back in the bakery where I worked.  That baby is a hundred years old, and has been in my family for generations… if you can bring him to me, I'll bake you the finest bread you've ever had.
dialogue.accepted: Take care of yourself out there.  And listen, when you bring my sourdough back, I don't want to see a scratch on him, you understand?
dialogue.rejected: I can understand why you think you wouldn't want to risk your life for a bread starter.  You haven't tried that bread.
dialogue.advice: He'll be in the right-hand fridge, in a jar with a picture of the Millennium Falcon on it.
dialogue.inquire: So, you seen my sourdough starter?
dialogue.success: Oh, you will not regret this.  He may not look like much, but he's got it where it counts, kid.  It's gonna take me a few days to revive him after being abandoned so long, but he'll be operational soon and then you can come back for some real bread.
dialogue.success_lie: This ain't it.
dialogue.failure: I am not sure if I'm gonna make it through the Cataclysm without my special jar of goop.

data.description: This crusty old jar has a glow-in-the-dark millennium falcon decal on the side, and a label that reads, "Landough Calrisean.  Dana's.  Do not touch on pain of death".  It's been abandoned for some time and doesn't look like it could be readily salvaged as a sourdough culture, but maybe an experienced sourdough baker could manage it.
This round loaf of bread has a thick, dark crust, and smells very enticing.

data.//: Draco is a middle-aged musician, and generally a pretty nice guy.  He's always been a wanderer and this isn't his first time living basically homeless.
Use this flag to indicate if the player sold weed recently to Draco.

dynamic_line.yes: Always good to see you, friend.
dynamic_line.no: Well now, good to see another new face!  Welcome to the center, friend, I'm Draco.

responses.text: Hi, Draco, how are you doing?
Hi again, Draco, nice to see you too.
Hi again, Draco, nice to see you too.
Hi Draco, nice to meet you.  I gotta go though.
Hi Draco, nice to see you too.  I gotta go though.

data.dynamic_line: Nice to meet you too.  What brings you to these parts?  Got any stories to share?  Happy ones, hopefully… we've had our fill of sadness around here.

responses.text: What about you, how're you doing?
Yeah, it's tough everywhere.  Well, bye.

data.dynamic_line: Well, look at you.  Asking after random folks like some sort of shepherd!  No, don't take offense now… I mean it well.  We could use more folks askin' after other folks.  I figure it makes the world go round, now, more than ever.  I'm well, friend, considering I have both of my legs and much of my health left to me.  A bit of pain in the back, but can't really complain much if that's the worst of it, right?  You look like you've had a story of your own to tell, just getting here.  I'm writing it in my imagination right now.  Fought through countless hordes, run ragged, chased at every turn, yeah, no thank-you any more of that for me!

responses.text: What about you, what's your story?

data.dynamic_line: Oh you don't have time for all that, do you?  Well, I'll give you the short version.  I've gotten kinda tired of it in the telling.  Frankly, it's not as heroic, not as inspiring, not as tragic, and certainly not as funny as some of the tales around here.  But it's mine, ya know?  I'm a musician.  Guitar's my baby.  You like folk and the blues, friend?  Well, that was my bag and I sure could please my own ear with em, anyway.  Folks who's bein' generous might also say it pleased theirs.  Problem is, I seem to be between guitars right now, you know?  Temporarily guitar-light, if you get my saying.  Problem is, in the run for my life, I had to use old Jasmine as a bit of a billy club.  Had to curb some rowdy dudes on my way here.  It was her or me, you understand?  You wouldn't begrudge a man breakin' his instrument to save his life, would ya?

responses.text: I think I would've done the same.  Nobody around here has a guitar?
Yes, yes I would… you monster.

data.dynamic_line: Would you believe that they don't!  Not a one in the whole place.  Well, maybe downstairs, but that's a different matter, isn't it?  Say, you're not planning on sticking around, right?  You're a free-roller, not a settler, seems like to me.  Don't know if I could beg or cajole you into maybe keepin' an ear out for a new guitar for me?  There gotta still be plenty out there not gettin' any love these days.  Whattya say?  Help an old man play some blues?  Would be good to have some real music around this place.  Be good for PEOPLE, you know what I'm sayin'?

responses.text: Where would we be without music?
You're aware that the world has ended, right?  I've got real problems to deal with.  You're on your own.

data.dynamic_line: Let me ask you something.  What type are you?

responses.text: I'll tell you what type I am.

data.dynamic_line: You know, what kinda person are you?  What motivates you?

responses.text: I'll tell you what type I am.

data.dynamic_line: So then, what type are you?

responses.text: I want to see it all.
The 'doesn't have time for this' type.

data.dynamic_line: Me too!  You can understand how folks be wantin' some liveliness in these times.  Some music sure would help with that.  Damn, I miss it.  All I hear is those MP3 players with their tin-can drum machines and whiny vocals.  Help me find a guitar and we'll really get this place smokin'!

responses.text: It's called dub-step and I like it.  Goodbye, old man.

data.dynamic_line: Me too!  Times are hard for folks and that's no laughing matter.  People need some normality in these times.  Some reminders of how things used to be.  I think a sing-along or two could do folks good.

responses.text: I don't need to hear amateur-hour karaoke around here.  Goodbye.

data.dynamic_line: Me too!  I did stand-up comedy at a club once.  Well, outside a club anyway.  You know what'd be funny?  Next time one of those stupid ferals starts running around chasing after a squirrel or something, if I had me a guitar I could play the Benny Hill tune and get everybody crackin' up.  Places needs some laughter badly.

responses.text: Yeah, wouldn't be so funny when Zed heard all the sound and broke in.  Be responsible.

data.dynamic_line: Me too.  It's fight a stay afloat in these times.  Some music would lift all spirits, though, don't you think?

responses.text: Can you play heavy metal on an acoustic guitar?
Boring.  I'm going to go destroy something.

data.dynamic_line: Me too!  For now, anyway, that's not really possible for me.  I mean, I guess you know better than me about that.  Man, I used to travel all around.  Saw halfa the States with my guitar on my back.  Now, though, well, I think I'll stay inside til this all flies over.

responses.text: Maybe I could help with something?
Well then, I'll leave you here where it's safe.

dynamic_line.yes: My savior!  My patron of the arts!  You're always welcome here, friend.
dynamic_line.no: Man, just imagine what I could do with a new guitar.

responses.text: Let's talk about getting you that guitar.
I've been thinking about that deal you mentioned.
Anything you buying or selling, by chance?

data.dynamic_line: Well now, my friend-o!  You just asked a mighty fine question.  Folks have been missing the little things in life.  New shoes, new cellphones, can't exactly go shopping, or, well, I guess you sorta can, if you mind the broken glass.  I left my wallet in an outdoorsman's store when I 'bought' this warmer coat.  Figured that's kinda it, you know?  It didn't matter anymore.  I don't think my insurance's going to pay out for any health care I get now.  I did what you see in the movies though, I rolled a joint with a hundred dollar bill.  Ended up coughing and rerolling it in regular paper though.  Was too harsh.  Just letting you know in case you get the smart idea of trying it.
Say, I don't mean to get you in any trouble or nothing, if any folks still care about that, but you haven't seen any green around town, have ya?

responses.text: Oh yeah, some people've been growing it in their basements.
I'm not comfortable with where this is going.

data.dynamic_line: Where you say you're from again?  You're not as worldly as you look.  I'm talking about weed.  Marijuana.  Wondered if you've happened upon any.

responses.text: Right, of course I knew that!  There's tons of the stuff out there for the taking.

data.dynamic_line: Hey, don't get all serious on me all of a sudden.  It helps me relax.  Lubricates my joints.  Eases the pain, ya know?  Makes every day a bit more bearable.

dynamic_line.yes: Yeah, no worries, though.  I'm good at the moment.  Ask me again later and maybe I'll have scrounged up some more cash for you.
dynamic_line.no: Amazing!  My lucky day.  Let's see here.  What can I offer… I can scrounge up some Merch bucks for, say, five joints or joints-worth of the good stuff.

responses.text: You have yourself a deal.  Here's the marijuana.
You have yourself a deal.  Here's the marijuana.
You have yourself a deal.  Here's some joints.
You have yourself a deal.  Here's some joints.
Oh, alright.  I'll be back later with the goods.

data.dynamic_line: Well, let me know when you have.  I'm not going anywhere.

responses.text: I'm not your drug dealer, buddy.

data.dynamic_line: Sold!  Thanks for helping me out, friend.

dialogue.describe: Yeah, sure, imagine how things would be if we had some live music around here?  I don't know how much I could thank you, though, if you're looking for payment.  You'd sure be improving the mood, though.
dialogue.offer: I just want a functional acoustic guitar.  Preferably one that hasn't been used to cave in any zombie skulls.
dialogue.accepted: Great!  We'll be makin' music in no time!
dialogue.rejected: Oh well.  I understand your reluctancy… I guess.
dialogue.advice: Well, I'll let you in on a little secret.  Guitars COULD be found at a music store.  Let that one sink in a bit.
dialogue.success: Hell yeah, bud!  You just made a lot of people really happy!  In thanks, I'll have enough cash to offer you more recompense for our little dealings.
dialogue.success_lie: Huh.  This… is something, isn't it.
dialogue.failure: No worries.  They don't grow from trees, but we have time.

data.//: A welder, culturally muslim but only recently practicing since the Cataclysm has made her rethink her connections to her family's religion
common talk responses

responses.text: I'm trying to put a cleanup crew together to tidy up the back room.  Can you help?
How did you wind up here at the center?
Hey, you free for a bit of teaching?
Is there anything I can do to help you out?

yes: Good to see you're still around.
dynamic_line.no: Oh, hey, a new face.  Hi, I'm Fatima.  Just visiting I hope?  It's nice to meet new people but there are no beds to share.

responses.text: Nice to meet you too, Fatima.  I'm just passing through.
I'm afraid I can't talk right now.

data.dynamic_line: Well, cool.  Anything I can help you with?
Oh, you know, the usual.  Trapped in a tight space with a bunch of strangers getting along tenuously at best.  Good times, good times.

Before <the_cataclysm> I had just finished welding school actually, and was about to start looking for a job.  That was fun, being a young Muslim woman in a Massachusetts trade college, let me tell you.

responses.text: Welding seems like a pretty non-traditional occupational choice; is there a story there?

data.dynamic_line:
You'd be surprised actually!  Metal art has been part of Muslim traditions for years, although that's not why I got into it.  I'm not a very traditional girl.  My parents aren't very traditional either, but my grandparents are really old fashioned and strict.  My sister came out as gay and they made her life really hard; mom and dad thought she should keep it secret, but she didn't believe in that.  I always loved mechanics and working with my hands, so when they started harassing my parents about getting my sister and I married off to nice men so we'd stop being so immoral, I decided to pick a job I liked that would bother them as much as possible.  It was a good choice, not only did it make them livid but I love welding.  I love the feel of standing back and looking at my work, knowing I took a few chunks of scrap metal and made them into something useful.  I love how it feels to make it fit together perfectly.  It just puts me at peace.

I… I do hope my grandparents are okay though.  They were old fashioned, and they made choices I didn't like, but they were family and I still have sweet memories of them from when I was little.  I've had to do a lot more thinking about God since <the_cataclysm>, and while I'd never agree with the decisions they made, I understand more why they thought they had to make them.  They just wanted the whole family to share their relationship with God, in their messed up way.

responses.text: Welding comes up a lot in my life.  Do you think you could teach me?

dynamic_line.yes: Sure.  As agreed, 25 merch, .

no.no: Sure, I could teach you the basics, I'll have to charge you though.  Let's say, 5 merch for a teaching session, plus a bit in trade depending on how in-depth you're looking for?
no.yes: Sure, I could teach you the basics, it'll cost you merch though.  Since you helped me out, I can shave a bit off the price, let's say 4 merch, plus a bit in trade depending on how in-depth you're looking for?

responses.//: 5 merch if player has not bartered nor finished mission
4 merch if player has not bartered but has done the mission
3 merch if player has successfully bartered price down

responses.text: [BARTER] That's still pretty steep, I risked my neck out there for your book.  Can't you manage a little lower?

data.dynamic_line: Hey, I appreciate that, but I know what I've got, and I can make good money with that time.  Sorry, my price stands.
Oh, fine, you weasel.  I suppose I can manage for 3 notes.  I seriously can't go lower though, we'll be using up my resources and time and I gotta pay for the gas and the food somehow.

I was on my way to visit my parents back in Burlington, waiting at a bus station, when the evacuation notices started sounding.  I'd been a little out of touch for a bit and didn't realize how bad the rioting was getting.  When my bus arrived it got repurposed into an evacuation vehicle, and took me here.  I… I didn't used to be very religious, it's just something I was born to, but since this happened I've been thinking a lot more about God, and how grateful I am for His help in surviving.  With things still so difficult, it helps to know He's got some plan for me.

Anyway, mine was the second bus to arrive, and they were just getting some triage and processing stuff set up.  I was put in charge of helping with the wounded, along with Uyen.  Things went a little strange later on… one of the women doing triage and processing had a bit of a hang-up about particular, um, colors of people being allowed into the center.  She claimed to have lost our 'papers', along with a lot of other peoples'.  Thankfully because we'd helped so many we were able to argue that they couldn't leave us out, but there was no space left downstairs by the time we got that sorted, so here we are.

dynamic_line.no: It's tense here.  I know I'd feel a lot better if I had something to do with my skills, or even if I just had a quiet place to pray sometimes.  I feel a bit self-conscious praying in the common areas.  Jenny was talking about some project ideas she had that could get me doing my job again, but I admit I'm pretty nervous about going outside.
dynamic_line.yes: Things are still tense, but I've been busy lately.  Jenny's had her project going and got me started helping her out with it, and for some reason that seems to have been the tipping point: I'm getting chances to do a lot more welding work now.  It's helping.  I feel a bit self-conscious praying in the common areas, and of course, we don't go outside if we can help it.

name.str: Find a copy of the Quran

dialogue.describe: I could use a bit of help to find a copy of the Quran.
dialogue.offer: I feel silly asking this, but here goes.  I've never been really into reading holy books and stuff like that.  I usually went to the mosque on Friday, and I try to pray five times a day but I hardly ever manage it.  I guess I'm not a very good Muslim, but with all that's happened I would really love to have a copy of the Quran to read.  This seems like a time to get back in touch with God, you know?
dialogue.accepted: Thank you.  I'll see if I can save up a little reward for you.
dialogue.rejected: That's okay.  Thanks for offering.
dialogue.advice: It's not as common as the bible, but you should be able to find copies in most libraries and bookstores, or in religious buildings.  Make sure you get the translated version, I can't read Arabic!
dialogue.success: Thank you so much.  Just having a copy to keep at hand does actually feel pretty comforting.  I did a few extra rounds of chores and saved the proceeds for if you managed this, here you go.  It's not much but I hope it helps.
dialogue.success_lie: What good does this do me?
dialogue.failure: It's okay.  I don't know how much comfort I'd have found in an old book anyway.

data.//: Garry is a Stan's older brother.  He's grateful he's made it to help support his brother, but he's very worried about Stan.
common talk responses

responses.text: I'm trying to put a cleanup crew together to tidy up the back room.  Can you help?

dynamic_line.no: Hi.  Hi there.  I'm Garry, Garry Villeneuve.

responses.text: Hi Garry, nice to meet you.  I gotta go though.
Hi Garry.  I can't stay to talk.

data.dynamic_line: Nice to meet you too.  Are you staying here, or something?

responses.text: No, I'm a traveler.  What's up with you?
Nope, in fact I'm leaving right now.

data.dynamic_line: Doing my best to keep going in the face of… everything.  Not getting far.

Before the apocalypse I was an electrician.  Boris here is my brother-in-law, and we were a decent contractor team.  When the evacuations sounded, we left together with our… with our families.  We got stuck into a crowded evac shelter, then onto a crowded bus.  Then… everything went wrong.  The bus was attacked, destroyed.  Nearly everyone died.  A few of us made it back… not enough.
Yes.  My wife, Linda… thrown from the bus.  She didn't make it.  And… and my nephew, Ash, Boris and Stan's son.  We got him here, but there wasn't anything we could do.  Internal injuries.

It's tense here, but I don't know.  Stan, Boris and I have been pretty insular.  I guess we'd better get to know some of the others here eventually.  It feels it should be a temporary stop, but it's starting to look like we'll be here for the long term.  If we live that long.

data.//: Guneet is the Singhs' sixteen year old son.  Like his parents, he is wracked with survivor's guilt for his family having made it out intact.
common talk responses

responses.text: I'm trying to put a cleanup crew together to tidy up the back room.  Can you help?

dynamic_line.no: Oh, hello.  I don't think I've seen you around before.  I'm Guneet, people call me Gunny.

responses.text: Hi Gunny, nice to meet you.  I gotta go though.
Hi Gunny.  I can't stay to talk.

data.dynamic_line: I guess we're still doing that stuff?  Cool.  Nice to meet you too.  What's up?

I was in high school, you know.  Most of the way through my junior year.  "My story"?  I got on a bus with my parents, the bus crashed, and everyone died except a few people, most of whom are crammed into this little shelter now.  Who knows when we're getting out.

It sucks in here, there's no two ways about it.  People don't talk to us because we wear turbans and we still have each other.  They think because we're still together, we didn't lose anything.  My dad believes it, too, and I think my mom's on the fence.

data.//: Jenny Forcette is an experienced mechanical engineer.  Like the other refugees in the center, she's terrified of the outside world.  Unlike many, she has some ideas what to do about it.
Use this flag to indicate if the player has met this NPC before.
common talk responses

responses.text: I'm trying to put a cleanup crew together to tidy up the back room.  Can you help?
How's everything going with that defense system?
Tell me a bit about your background.
Are you free to teach me anything today?
Can you tell me anything about the other refugees here?

dynamic_line.no: Hi there.  Haven't see you around here before.  I'm Jenny, Jenny Forcette.

responses.text: Nice meeting you.  What are you doing on that computer?
Hi, Jenny.  What are you up to these days?
Nice meeting you.  I'd best get going, though.
Sorry Jenny, I can't stay to chat.

data.dynamic_line: I'm puttering around, I always have stuff on the go.  Gotta keep busy, keep my mind off stuff, you know?

Me?  I trained at MIT in mechanical engineering, I worked for a long time as senior engineer at Marduk Thermal in Rhode Island.  It was a good job, but I landed my dream gig at Boston Dynamics and moved up north to start there.  I had just finished my orientation and was going to start work when the riots started.  Just my damn luck.

responses.text: That's impressive, but there must be more to you than just your job.
You must know some great stuff.  Can you teach me anything?
Sorry about your luck.  What were you saying before?

data.dynamic_line: Ha!  You must not know many engineers, hey?  I guess there's more to me than engineering, but most of my hobbies come back to it one way or the other.  It's not that I live for my work, doing engineering for a heating company wasn't some great dream, but when I got home I'd putter with the projects I wanted to do instead of the ones they made me do.  You know?  And of course, I had my friends and things, we'd go out or hang out and play board games and stuff.  Maybe some day I'll get a board game group started up here, although there's nothing wrong with the card games we've got now.  Plus I don't think Zombicide would hold the same interest for me as it used to.

Huh.  I guess I can teach you a bit, but you'd have to be like, my on-the-job apprentice.  It'll cost you a bit depending on what you want to learn.  Do you know anything about electronics, computers, or mechanics already?

responses.text: [SKILL <2] No, that's why I want you to teach me.
[INTELLIGENCE 10] No, but I'm a fast learner.
Um, you know what?  Nevermind.  What were you saying?

data.dynamic_line: All right, fine.  Grab some tools and do as I tell you.
I'm sorry, I don't have the time to teach someone who can't pull their weight, I just don't.

dynamic_line.no: I recently came into possession of this mold for making high-caliber air rifle bullets.  I'm kinda working on a design that would use them to protect the base.  Got a long way to go, though.
dynamic_line.yes: About a month ago, I got a mold for making high-caliber air rifle bullets.  I've been designing some turrets that would use a central air system to power pneumatic rifle turrets around the center.  It's a lot easier than trying to make gunpowder!

responses.text: Tell me more about your project.

dynamic_line.no: Well, these things are a standard .30 caliber.  They should be compatible with any similar rifle barrel.  It would be pretty easy to repurpose some rifle parts into large air weapons that we could use without relying on gunpowder, and without so much noise.  I'm still drawing up an actual design though, I have a bunch of features I want.  Ask me again in a couple weeks and I'll give you some more info.
dynamic_line.yes: They're pretty big.  This isn't something you'd carry around with you.  They fire .30 cal bullets using compressed air that we'd make inside the basement and then pipe up to individual storage tanks for the guns that would be good for a few hundred shots each.  The design should be capable of auto or semi-auto fire, at a range that's pretty comparable to a gunpowder-based weapon.  It takes out some of the most limited parts of ranged weapons: no gunpowder, no brass casings, just lead that we melt into my mold.  It's not soundless, but it's not as loud as a chemical weapon.  There are tons of advantages.  Only trouble is, I can't convince the Free Merchants to give me the parts I need.

responses.text: Is there some way I can help you get the stuff you need?

dynamic_line.no: Things are coming along.  I have a lot of studying to do before I know how to fix my design issues, but the book you brought definitely has everything I need.  Now that I've got some progress to show, administration is much more willing to help me get the parts I need.  You've been a great gofer, but I can probably handle the rest on my own.  Check back in a week or two!

yes.no: I'm really making headway.  We've done some live demonstrations with a working device, and now it's just a matter of manufacturing a few of them.  We should be ready for release in a week or two.
yes.yes: It's finally ready!  The pipes are laid to the first patch of ground we'll set turrets up in and I'd like for you to join me to go inspect how they are working.  I'll let you know when I'm ready to go.
yes.//: After content freeze remove last sentence on var yes, create mission to nearby field, create air powered turrets, use update mapgen to have some corpses that will rise near the turrets as you approach, create followup followup missions that add additional turrets to nearby fields as time goes on.

dynamic_line.no: Living here?  Yeah, I guess I live here now.  It's… it's weird.  We're crowded into this tiny space, I don't know these people, but we're sharing bathrooms and we've all been through the same stuff.  It's not great.  At night we can hear the <zombies> outside, and we all just lie there awake, thinking the same things but too scared to talk about it.

yes.no: It's been over a month now, so I guess I'm starting to get used to it.  Things were pretty rough after Sean died, but it wasn't our first big loss and it won't be the last I guess.  I've made a couple friends, and in a weird way we're all like family.  We were all hoping they'd let us downstairs sooner than this though.  We're never quite sure if there's going to be enough food to go around.  I'm really hoping I can lose myself in this project.  Still haven't had a good night's sleep since <the_cataclysm>.

There's good and there's bad.  We're all pretty sick of being cooped up in here for months, never knowing if there's going to be food to eat or not.  It's starting to look like they're never going to let us go down to the secure basement, and none of us have slept well since we were brought in.  We know we've got it pretty good… we're safe, we're alive.  It's just, like, what kind of life are we even living?
yes.yes: It's getting bad.  We've been stuck in here for months, nothing changing, nothing improving.  We can't go outside, we don't have enough to eat, and we didn't choose to be with each other.  I don't know how long we can stay like this before somebody snaps.

The Borichenkos are their own sweet brand of messed up, like all of us.  The Singhs have each other, and keep mostly to themselves.  Vanessa and I don't see eye to eye, but I'm still glad she's here.  Uyen and Rhyzaea are always bickering about leadership decisions, as if they made those kind of calls.  What did you want to know?
dynamic_line.no: Well, there's a bunch of us.  We're starting to form a bit of a community.  Fatima and I work together a fair bit, and I've been hanging out with Dana, Draco, and Aleesha quite a lot.  I don't know the Borichenko bunch, the Singhs, Vanessa, Uyen, or Rhyzaea quite as well, but we've talked.  What did you want to know?

data.dynamic_line: They run this place, and they don't run a charity.  We get paid for working around the place, maintaining it, what have you, and we trade cash for food.  The thing is, supply and demand and all… there's a lot more cash than food around.  It's easier to buy a laptop than a piece of beef jerky, and there's no sign of that getting better.  The balance is way off right now, a hard day of work barely gets you enough to fill your belly.  I shouldn't bitch too much though.  I don't know much better way to run it, although rumor is that the folks living downstairs have it a lot easier than we do.  I try not to think too much on that.

responses.text: What was it you said earlier?

data.dynamic_line: Fatima's a sweety, but she's a total dork.  I know, I know, it's backwards for the engineer to call the heavy duty mechanic a nerd, but hey.  I call it like it is.  She and I have been doing some odd jobs around the upstairs here, fixing up old machinery and things.

responses.text: What was it you said earlier?

data.dynamic_line: Well, Dana lost her baby right after <the_cataclysm>, in a bus rollover.  She was lucky to make it out alive.  She and Pedro had one of the rougher trips here, I guess.  We just kinda click as friends, I'm grateful there's someone else here I can really get along with.  Her husband, Pedro, is still pretty shell-shocked.  He doesn't talk much.  I like him though, when he opens up he's just hilarious.  Draco is just a cantankerous old fart who hasn't actually got old yet, give him twenty years and he'll be there.  I like grumpy people.  We also have pretty similar taste in music.  Aleesha's a sweet kid, and we've all kind of adopted her, but she seems to hang out with me and Dana the most.  She's a great artist, and she's full of crazy ideas.  I guess I like her because of all of us, she seems to have the most hope that there's a future to be had.

responses.text: What was it you said earlier?

dynamic_line.yes: I didn't get to know Boris, Garry, and Stan so well for the first while.  They kinda kept to themselves.  Boris and Stan had just lost their son, you know. They probably do the most to pull their weight around here whenever there's work to be done.
dynamic_line.no: Boris and Stan are married, I guess.  They kinda keep to themselves, they seem a bit standoffish if you ask me.  Garry is Stan's brother, I think, but I'm not totally sure.  He seems nice enough, but he's a man of few words.  I can't get a good bead on them.  I've learned not to pry too much though.

responses.text: What was it you said earlier?

dynamic_line.no: I really can't get a bead on them.  They never really talk to anyone outside of their little family group, they just sit in their own spot and speak Punjabi.  They always seem nice, and they do their share, they just don't have any social connection.

responses.text: What was it you said earlier?

dynamic_line.yes: Vanessa… I'm doing my best, I really am, but we just do not get along.  One of these days one of us is probably going to brain the other with a tire iron, and I'm just grateful I spend more time around the tire irons.  Uyen and Rhyzaea are both excellent people, and I genuinely like them, but I can't stand this ongoing political bullshit they've got going on.  Alonso is just a… he's… there's no polite word for what he is.  A lot of the others are fine with it, and okay, sure, I guess.  John is a walking stereotype, but he's a great poker buddy.  I admit I kinda like him.
dynamic_line.no: Vanessa… well, she's nice, I guess.  I gotta say, she kinda drives me nuts, but we're in this together so I try not to be too harsh.  Uyen and Rhyzaea both seem to want to run the show here, but I try to stay out of those politics and just focus on building stuff.  I don't see much good coming of it.  Alonso is fine, he's clearly interested in me, and also in every other single person here.  Not my thing, in a group this small.  John is a walking stereotype, I imagine there must be more depth to him, but I haven't seen it yet.

Thanks.  No, really, thank you.  Others have gone through so much I feel like we should suck it up, but Rhy says we should let ourselves mourn properly and she seems to know her stuff.

From the bus?  A few of us made it in the end; the Singh family were on that bus with us.  We were some of the last refugees to arrive.  They put us into a room for processing, where a bunch of the wounded were being handled as best as they could manage.  They were short staffed though, and they missed one.  We all thought he was just having a nap, but he wasn't, and when he got back up as a zombie, there was a huge panic.  Gunshots in a small, crowded room, and trampling… it was really ugly.  We were close to the door and managed to get out right away, but then a couple panicking people closed the place off and left innocent people in there for what seemed like ages, calling it an 'outbreak'.  By the time leveler heads prevailed, there weren't many people left in there to recover.

data.dynamic_line: Yes, I can buy 500 mL or 3 L glass jars at the moment.
